claims.statement: For every fixed nonzero t, the supremum of |E exp(i t X^2)| over probability densities f with 0<=f<=1 is exactly 1. Hence no positive-power law-uniform pointwise decay estimate can hold over this class.
claims.scope: Single real random variable; density cap 1; compactly supported indicator witnesses allowed.
claims.full_target_effect: Refutes only a proposed Fourier sublemma, not the quadratic-form bounded-density conjecture.

claims.statement: If X has probability density <=1, then the density g of X^2 satisfies ||g||_{3/2}<=2 and ||E exp(i t X^2)||_{L^3(dt)} <= 2(2pi)^{1/3}. More generally lambda X^2+beta X has L^3 characteristic norm <=2(2pi)^{1/3}|lambda|^{-1/3}.
claims.scope: Arbitrary real probability density bounded by 1; no support, moment, smoothness or shape assumptions.

claims.statement: For independent X_i with densities <=1, every coordinate-diagonal Q=sum lambda_i X_i^2 with at least three |lambda_i|>=1 has a bounded continuous density with ||p_Q||_infinity<=8.
claims.scope: All dimensions; arbitrary coefficient signs, repetitions and remaining coefficients; independent coordinate basis aligned with Q.

claims.statement: For Q=x^T A x, if three coordinate indices have |A_ii|>=1 and zero pairwise cross coefficients among them, then Q(X) has density <=8 for all independent coordinate laws with densities <=1.
claims.scope: Arbitrary remaining matrix entries; proof conditions on all other coordinates and uses linear-term-uniform L^3 bounds.

claims.statement: Prove a dimension-free L^1_t bound for the product-measure quadratic oscillatory integral whenever the symmetric phase matrix has at least three eigenvalues of absolute value >=1; this would imply the full target by Fourier inversion.
claims.scope: Full rotated target; arbitrary product densities bounded by 1 and arbitrary linear term.
